---
title: "Sequential models"
---

Sequential models make predictions from ordered observations. We begin with a
fixed window of the series' own past, then ask what changes when the model can
also use a known input and learn a nonlinear state.

## 1. Autoregressive models

Use real hourly transformer oil-temperature measurements to see what changes
when an autoregressive model is allowed to look back one hour, several hours,
one day, or one week.

[Explore autoregressive model order](01-autoregressive-models-explorer.qmd)

[Work through the notebook](01-autoregressive-models.html)

## 2. Input--response forecasting with the Silverbox benchmark

Use the Silverbox nonlinear-system benchmark to compare three forecasting
models on the same held-out input--response experiment: one that uses past
responses, one that also uses a known input, and one that learns a nonlinear
recurrent state.

[Explore AR, ARX, and recurrent models](02-silverbox-arx-rnn-explorer.qmd)

[Work through the notebook](02-silverbox-arx-rnn.html)

## 3. Backpropagation through time

Use a deliberately small delayed-cue task to unroll a scalar RNN, calculate
the gradient through every recurrent transition, and see how repeated local
gradient factors can vanish or explode.

[Explore backpropagation through time](03-bptt-explorer.qmd)

[Work through the notebook](03-backpropagation-through-time.html)
